classification.difficultyReason: Apply the triangle area formula using given perpendicular lengths, including external heights and matching parallel-line cues.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of these triangles.

spec.description: Tilted right triangle with the right angle at the right vertex; its two perpendicular sides are labelled 2.4 m and 1 m.
spec.mathematics: The labelled sides meet at a right angle and provide the base and perpendicular height.
spec.answerVisibility: Show both measurements and the right-angle marker; withhold the supplied area.

spec.description: Oblique triangle with a horizontal base labelled 3 mm and an external vertical height labelled 2 mm. Dashed red lines extend the base to the altitude foot.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular height is 2 mm; the triangle's base is the solid 3 mm segment, excluding its dashed extension.
spec.answerVisibility: Show the given lengths, dashed construction and right-angle marker; withhold the supplied area.

spec.description: Triangle with a horizontal upper base labelled 7 km and an opposite vertex below and to the right. A dashed red base extension meets the dashed vertical 7 km height at a right angle.
spec.mathematics: The solid upper side is the 7 km base; the external perpendicular height is also 7 km.
spec.answerVisibility: Show both 7 km measurements and the external construction; withhold the supplied area.

spec.description: Triangle with a vertical left base labelled 2 cm and its opposite vertex above and to the right. A dashed red extension of the base meets the horizontal 1.3 cm height at a right angle.
spec.mathematics: The vertical 2 cm side is the base; its perpendicular horizontal height is 1.3 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Show the two measurements and the external construction; withhold the supplied area.

spec.description: Triangle with left, lower-middle and upper-right vertices. The upper sloping side is labelled 10 m. Matching arrows identify that side and the dashed parallel line through the lower vertex. A dashed red 4 m perpendicular joins the upper-right vertex to the parallel line.
spec.mathematics: The 4 m perpendicular distance between the parallel lines is the height corresponding to the 10 m side.
spec.answerVisibility: Show the full parallel-line construction, both matching arrows, both measurements and the right-angle marker; withhold the supplied area.

answer.worked:
The parallel-line markings show that $4\,\mathrm{m}$ is the perpendicular height for the $10\,\mathrm{m}$ base.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{10\times4}{2}\\A&=20\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with upper-left, lower-left and lower-right vertices. The long descending side is labelled 5 m. Matching arrows mark it parallel to the dashed line through the lower-left vertex. A dashed red perpendicular labelled 1.7 m runs down-left from the upper-left vertex to that line.
spec.mathematics: The 1.7 m perpendicular separation of the parallel lines is the height corresponding to the 5 m side.
spec.answerVisibility: Show the full parallel construction, both matching arrows, both measurements and the right-angle marker; withhold the supplied area.

answer.worked:
The parallel-line markings show that $1.7\,\mathrm{m}$ is the perpendicular height for the $5\,\mathrm{m}$ base.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{5\times1.7}{2}\\A&=4.25\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\end{align*}$$
